title: A basis change preserves the universal incidence equation
statement: For any two finite bases b and b′ of a k-vector space V and linear map a:V→A into a commutative k-algebra, there are compatible k- and A-algebra isomorphisms of the corresponding multivariate polynomial rings. The A-algebra isomorphism carries Σ C(a(bᵢ))Xᵢ to Σ C(a(b′ⱼ))Xⱼ; compatibility means scalar extension of the k-coordinate change agrees with the A-coordinate change.

source.place: Tag 0G4F, proof; tensor-pullback and affine-coordinate details

proof.text: Use the dual bases and their symmetric-algebra polynomial presentations to construct the linear coordinate change. Extend coefficients from k to A by polynomial evaluation; the inverse coordinate change gives an inverse after extension. Evaluation on variables proves compatibility and the universal incidence equation.

theorem exists_bertiniBasisCoordinateChange
    (k A : Type u) [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    {V : Type v} [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
    {I : Type w} {J : Type w'} [Fintype I] [Fintype J]
    (b : Module.Basis I k V) (b' : Module.Basis J k V) (a : V →ₗ[k] A) :
    ∃ (e : MvPolynomial I k ≃ₐ[k] MvPolynomial J k)
      (eA : MvPolynomial I A ≃ₐ[A] MvPolynomial J A),
      (∀ p, eA (map (algebraMap k A) p) = map (algebraMap k A) (e p)) ∧
      eA (∑ i, C (a (b i)) * X i) = ∑ j, C (a (b' j)) * X j
